solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Source of solar light, ardent in pop's unwrapped present

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, sitting within its letters
something unwrapped is opened out and disturbed, so its letters come out in a new order

parts.note: read as one word, pop with its S
ardent means burning or fiery
present, as in in attendance

explanation.surface: Dad is apparently giving an unwrapped present that radiates warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pop's' as a single word with its S; 'unwrapped' asks for it to be opened out and rearranged so it can hold the ardent word.
explanation.definitionFit: The photosphere is the visible luminous outer layer of the sun, from which its light is emitted.

clue.text: What supports springs? Pole holding belt in — right, possibly (11, two words)

indicators.note: a thing holding another keeps it inside, so one word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement among several, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone is putting a belt on a pole and wondering if that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The springs are not coiled metal on a pole but the suspension of a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A splinter bar is the crossbar on a carriage to which the traces are fixed and which carries the vehicle's springs.

clue.text: Showing taste, copy warm blanket

parts.note: sar is a Scots word for savour or taste
to ape is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: A tasteful knock-off of a cosy throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarape, or serape, is a brightly coloured woollen shawl or blanket worn in Mexico.

clue.text: Prince riding deer in India as customary action

indicators.note: a rider sits on top, so in a down answer the first item comes above the next

parts.note: Pr is the abbreviation for Prince
the axis is the spotted deer of India

explanation.surface: A maharajah out riding a deer, as royals traditionally do.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'riding' puts the prince above the deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxis means practice as opposed to theory, or an established habitual way of doing things.

clue.text: US footballers from eastern state clothed in e.g. cotton

indicators.note: being clothed in something means being wrapped inside it

parts.note: linen covers cloth goods such as cotton sheets and shirts
ME is the abbreviation for Maine, a state in the eastern USA

explanation.surface: American football players from New England dressed in cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Linemen are players in American football who line up on the line of scrimmage.

clue.text: Wild root vegetable our lot shovel up

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: we are our lot
a van is a winnowing shovel or fan

explanation.surface: Our gang digging up wild vegetables with spades.
explanation.definitionFit: Navew is an old name for the wild turnip or rape, a root crop.

clue.text: Maple in sample ornamental openwork

indicators.note: the tree's name is set inside the other word

parts.note: first part of try, to sample
Acer is the botanical genus of maples
last letter of try, to sample

explanation.surface: A specimen of maple wood carved into decorative fretwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Acer, the maple's botanical genus name, is a common crossword stand-in for the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracery is the interlaced decorative stonework in Gothic windows, or any similar delicate open pattern.

clue.text: Individual plant soak has enveloped before noon

indicators.note: to envelop something is to surround it completely

parts.note: first letter of ret, to soak flax
am means ante meridiem, before noon
rest of ret, to soak flax or hemp

explanation.surface: A gardener soaking a single plant in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Ret is the specialist word for soaking flax or hemp so the fibres loosen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramet is one independent member of a clone, a single plant grown vegetatively from a parent.

clue.text: Tough course in workshop taken up

indicators.note: the track word is put inside the other
in a down answer, taking up means lifting it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: first part of lab, a workshop
rut, a fixed course, ready to be read backwards
last letter of lab

explanation.surface: A hard training course held in a workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: RUT goes inside LAB, then the whole is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal and tough both describe something harsh, severe and hard to endure.

clue.text: Might one find Rome concealed with this, one miracle possibly

definitions.text: Might one find Rome concealed with this, one miracle possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise
the city sits hidden alongside the answer within the fodder, so it is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Could Rome be found hidden with a miraculous object?
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: ONE MIRACLE rearranges as ROME plus the answer, so remove ROME. Legend says the ancile fell from heaven, a miracle, and Rome's safety depended on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancile was the sacred shield of ancient Rome, said to have fallen from the sky, on which the city's fate rested.

clue.text: Suicide? Not right — give ear, lilting air about one

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the single letter

parts.note: first part of hark, to listen
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a lilting tune moves in a swinging way, so the letters swing into a new order

parts.note: last letter of hark
taken as written

explanation.surface: A melancholy song about someone contemplating suicide.
explanation.walkthrough: HARK goes about I; then AIR is rearranged. 'Not right' signals that this is a corrupt spelling of hara-kiri.
explanation.definitionFit: Hari-kari is a common misspelling of hara-kiri, the Japanese ritual suicide by disembowelment, hence the note that it is not correct.

clue.text: Fixed engagement taking in East End, fashionable

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it inside, so the word holds the rest

parts.note: first letter of date, a social engagement
E is the abbreviation for east
a term is a limit or end
in means fashionable
rest of date, a social engagement

explanation.surface: A fixed date in London's East End for a stylish event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' reads as the London district but must be split into two words: east, and end in the sense of a limit or term.
explanation.definitionFit: Determinate means having exact, settled limits, so firmly fixed or definite.

clue.text: Worshipper hastened amid Christian text

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: first letter of OT, the Old Testament
ran means hurried or hastened
last letter of OT, the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A devotee rushing in among the Bible's pages.
explanation.definitionFit: An orant is a figure in early Christian art shown praying with arms raised, a worshipper.

clue.text: Hooded cape, capital when held by dancing girl

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within its grasp

parts.note: first part of alme, an Egyptian dancing girl
UC stands for upper case, capital letters
last letter of alme

explanation.surface: A dancer holding a capital city or wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is neither city nor money but UC, upper case, inside ALME, an Egyptian dancing girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An almuce, or amice, is a furred hood or hooded cape worn by clergy in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Language element to make heavy demands on old relative

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain them
eme is an obsolete word for uncle

explanation.surface: Learning a language puts a strain on an elderly family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxeme is in linguistics a minimal feature of grammatical arrangement, such as word order or stress.

clue.text: Large part of inner hunger, not significant

indicators.note: most of the inside is kept, with the outer and one more letter dropped

parts.note: appetite is hunger; its inside, without one more letter

explanation.surface: Feeling a small pang of hunger that hardly matters.
explanation.walkthrough: APPETITE loses its outer A and E, and then one P too.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit, from French for small, means minor or petty, as in petit larceny or petit jury.

clue.text: Tasteless water swallowed? It's certainly not bitter (8, two words)

indicators.note: what is swallowed goes inside, so one word ends up within the other

parts.note: first letter of stale, tasteless
wee is a childish word for urine
rest of stale, flat and tasteless

explanation.surface: Someone sipping flat water and declaring it not bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter here is the British style of hoppy beer, so a sweet ale is its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet ale is a malty beer without hops, the very opposite of the bitter served in British pubs.

clue.text: Reverse affirmations? It meant 'nuff said'

indicators.note: to reverse something is to run it backwards

parts.note: plural of yes

explanation.surface: Saying yes repeatedly until nothing more needs to be said.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesey is a Shakespearean interjection of uncertain sense, glossed as 'enough said' or 'let it pass'.

clue.text: Transaction involving rotter, to do with tenners

indicators.note: one thing involving another has it within, so one word wraps round the rest

parts.note: first part of deal, a transaction
a cad is a dishonourable man
rest of deal

explanation.surface: A dodgy deal with a scoundrel involving ten-pound notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenners look like banknotes but mean groups of ten, such as decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadal means relating to a decade or to tens, groups of ten.

clue.text: Dancing Scotsman? A warbler in the grass

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who dances a Scottish reel
second meaning: the grasshopper warbler, named for its reeling song

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition looks like a singer lying in the grass, but it is the grasshopper warbler.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person performing a Highland reel and also the grasshopper warbler, whose trill resembles a fishing reel.

clue.text: Make round article of clay

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first word goes about the second

parts.note: first part of earn, to make money
the definite article
last letter of earn

explanation.surface: A potter shaping a round object out of clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make round article' suggests a potter's pot, but make is EARN and article is THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthen describes things made of baked clay or earth, such as earthenware pots.

clue.text: Pole aforetime, Nancy down under

parts.note: the word shortened to its first two letters, an abbreviation Azed allows here
once means formerly

explanation.surface: A Polish man from the past, a Nancy now living in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; PO is a rare abbreviation of it, which even the blogger could not source.
explanation.definitionFit: Poonce is Australian slang for an effeminate man, the same sense as the dated British slur nancy.

clue.text: Wild ox once enveloped in charm, creature roaming the plains?

indicators.note: something enveloped in another is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: first letter of obi, a charm or fetish in obeah
ure is an old word for the urus, an extinct wild ox
rest of obi

explanation.surface: An extinct wild ox wrapped in charms, a beast of the open plains.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi or ourebi is a small African antelope living on grassy plains.

clue.text: Distinctive rabbit causing row with leaping mate

parts.note: to row with an oar

indicators.note: a leap in a down answer goes upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: a pal is a mate

explanation.surface: An odd-looking rabbit starts a quarrel with a hopping friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, a quarrel, but the clue wants the boating sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarlap is a rabbit whose ears stand out at right angles to the head, like oars.

clue.text: Crush middle of stomach in fine wool

indicators.note: the answer is found in the wool, read as the crush plus the letter

parts.note: a pash is a schoolgirl crush, short for passion

indicators.note: the central letter alone of the next word is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: Squeezing the belly into soft woollens.
explanation.definitionFit: Pashm is the fine underfleece of Tibetan goats from which pashmina and cashmere are made.

clue.text: Clever chap bags measure in old net

indicators.note: to bag something is to take it inside a bag, enclosing it

parts.note: first part of sage, a wise man
an en is a printer's measure
last letter of sage

explanation.surface: A smart fellow netting a fish, measured and kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagene is an obsolete word for a fishing net, related to seine.

clue.text: One tries to draw some money in Czechia including heart of resources

indicators.note: including means taking within, so the coin's name surrounds a letter

parts.note: first part of haler, a Czech coin

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter is kept

parts.note: the central letter of the nine
rest of haler, a hundredth of a koruna

explanation.surface: Someone trying to draw cash in Prague, with resources at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests drawing money or pictures, but here it means pulling a load.
explanation.definitionFit: A hauler is someone who pulls or hauls things, so tries to draw them along.

clue.text: Sandal one's in pained mostly, twice

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
one's letter is placed inside the first word

parts.note: hurt, pained, without its last letter
a means one
ached, pained, without its last letter
tells the solver to use the previous words two ways

explanation.surface: A sandal that hurts badly, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice' tells you to use 'pained mostly' two ways: HURT and ACHED, each cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A huarache is a Mexican sandal with a woven leather upper.

clue.text: Praise for some was swelling, filled with love

indicators.note: a thing filled with something has it inside

parts.note: first part of rose, rose up or swelled
love is zero in tennis, O
rest of rose

explanation.surface: Swelling with love in praise of someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For some' marks a dialect word: roose is Scots and northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: Roose is a dialect word meaning to praise or flatter, used by some speakers rather than all.

clue.text: Old time tart lowering her head somewhat

indicators.note: the first letter moves down a little, so the order of letters changes

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals bowing her head a little in shame.
explanation.walkthrough: The W, her head, drops two places down the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Howre is an old spelling of hour, a period of time.

clue.text: School basics about over after English clanger

indicators.note: after places the rest behind the first letter

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: about means round, so the basics surround the cricket letter

parts.note: part of the three Rs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
the last of the three Rs

explanation.surface: An English teacher dropping a clanger over the school basics.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is British slang for a conspicuous blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Middle of round includes damaged gut and defeat in shooting, …

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within
only the central letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the inner three of five letters

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A round fired into a damaged gut in a shootout.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgun is to beat an opponent by having more or better firepower.

clue.text: … Precluding need for one awkward ordeal?

definitions.note: the ellipsis carries on from the previous clue: outgunning precludes the need for a reload

indicators.note: something awkward is clumsy and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Winning a gunfight outright avoids an awkward pause mid-battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition joins on from the previous clue: defeat in shooting precludes need for one, that is, for a fresh load of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reload is a fresh charge of ammunition, which a winning shooter has no need of.

clue.text: Religious novice from part of the capital (not south-east)

parts.note: Chelsea is a district of London
SE is the abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A trainee monk from a London borough, though not the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a fashionable district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A chela is a disciple or pupil of a Hindu or Buddhist guru, a novice in religious training.

clue.text: Fine silk tissue snare damaged in value

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits within the value word

parts.note: taken as written
rest of set
first letter of set, to fix a value

clue.text: Part of smoker's wherewithal? Pierce panel in pieces

parts.note: taken as written
